artifact.reproducible_build: SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH is pinned to the commit date of HEAD and the setuptools build tree is removed before every build; scripts/linux/release_reproducibility.sh builds the wheel three times in a row and compares the digests (see campaigns/release/build_reproducibility.json)

reproducibility_check.method: three consecutive `python -m build --wheel --no-isolation` runs of the same tree with SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH pinned to the commit date of HEAD and the setuptools build tree removed before each run

artifact.shipped_content: the pdelab library (Python source) and the wheel metadata only; no configuration, data or artifact is included

source.note: the recorded revision is the commit the wheel was built from; the working tree was dirty at build time, so the wheel is not reproducible from the commit alone - it is reproducible from the working tree that was built, which is what the three-build reproducibility check measures (see artifact.reproducibility_check)

reproduction.command: pdelab doctor && pdelab solvers validate --system burgers
reproduction.note: the command was executed verbatim (from campaigns/release/fixtures/reproduction_command.txt) against the installed CLI, in the clean environment and from outside the source checkout. The numerical gate is driven through the installed CLI itself (`pdelab solvers validate --system burgers`), which prints the JSON report of the suite; the same path is exercised for allen_cahn by the clean-install verification.

solver_validation_cli.note: both CLI paths of `pdelab solvers validate` are exercised against the installed wheel, outside the source checkout; each must exit 0 and print a JSON report whose `passed` flag is true

learned_operators_vs_direct_numerical_st.statement: On these benchmarks the learned operators do NOT beat direct numerical stepping of the PDE. The parameter informed numerical baseline has a lower held-out rollout nRMSE than every learned operator of the cohort, by the factors listed below.
learned_operators_vs_direct_numerical_st.note: the numerical baseline is not parameter free and is not comparable with a learned model in terms of prior knowledge; it quantifies how much of the task is solvable by direct numerical integration.

burgers_residual_improvement_is_operator.statement: The Burgers residual improvement is a property of the declared residual operator, not of the model. Under the declared implicit-Euler (first order) residual the physics-regularized FNO improves on the data-only FNO (about +70% per seed); under the independently declared centred first-derivative residual it is WORSE on every seed (45% to 63% worse), and under that independent evaluator the reference solution has a LOWER residual than either learned model, i.e. the reference is more PDE-consistent than both models. Allen-Cahn improves under both evaluators.
burgers_residual_improvement_is_operator.note: the two evaluators are never mixed and are evaluated on the same support (the interior snapshot indices 1 .. T-2).

inference_memory_claim_is_peak_allocated.statement: The inference memory result is about PEAK ALLOCATED memory only. The peak allocated memory of the best variant falls by about 96% against the FP32 eager baseline, but the peak RESERVED memory rises by about 9% (the CUDA-graph private pool is larger than the eager allocator's working set), and the device-level free-memory reading is essentially unchanged. It is NOT a total device-memory saving and it is NOT a claim about the memory footprint of the model itself.

measured.artifact_caveat: memory_reduction_percent is the reduction in PEAK ALLOCATED memory during the measured steady-state region. It is NOT a reduction in total device memory: compare memory_reserved_reduction_percent, the persistent_* byte counts and the device-level free-memory observation for the two variants before drawing a device-memory conclusion.

inference_memory_claim_is_peak_allocated.note: the numbers are recomputed from the stored benchmark artifact of the declared inference reference run; the artifact itself carries the same caveat in its `memory_caveat` field.

measured_limitations.not_a_state_of_the_art_claim: the cohort is a single machine, three seeds per condition and two self-defined periodic benchmarks; the numbers are not a comparison against published work.

scope_statement: This is a LOCAL release artifact of a research prototype. It is NOT a claim of public deployment, NOT a claim of production serving readiness, and NOT a claim of novel state-of-the-art research. The wheel contains the library only; the datasets, the checkpoints and the run artifacts are not part of the bundle and must be regenerated from the source tree.
